Yesterdays -  Market Recap — Jan 26, 2026
SPY +0.51% | QQQ +0.44% | DIA +0.64%

Stocks edged higher Monday, kicking off Fed and Big Tech week with steady gains. Industrials carried the load while traders lightened up on tech ahead of a packed earnings slate. It wasn’t a big move, but considering what’s coming, green was good enough.

The dollar slid to a four‑month low after talk of coordinated yen support surfaced. That weaker USD helped U.S. multinationals (companies earning a lot overseas), boosting the Dow and S&P. Still, equity desks warned that sustained yen strength could hit profit margins, so traders took some chips off the table in Apple, Meta, and Microsoft before results.

Energy was a hot zone again — natural gas prices have doubled in just five sessions before chatter of a potential collapse cooled things off. Volatility there kept quants and commodity funds busy, but the broader market mostly ignored the fireworks.

Meanwhile, unrest in Minnesota and rising odds of a government shutdown (markets now pricing around 78%) pushed money toward safety trades. Gold topped $5,000/oz as risk‑parity funds worked to rebalance amid heavier defensive flows.

Takeaway:
A weaker dollar, wild energy swings, and creeping policy risk drove rotation into cyclicals while tech took a breather. With macro energy running hot and political noise picking up, all eyes turn to the Fed next.

 Tomorrow:
The Fed decision and megacap earnings drop — a one‑two combo that’ll set the tone for the rest of the week.
